title: Microtubule / Tubulin Multiscale Causal Theory — Molecular Dynamics to Neural Function
status: established cytoskeletal biology + project multiscale causal programme + explicitly gated quantum branch
abstract: The microtubule branch becomes scientifically valuable when treated as a multiscale causal inference problem rather than a direct jump from tubulin to consciousness. The established foundation is strong: microtubules are dynamic cytoskeletal polymers that regulate neuronal polarity, intracellular transport, morphology and many aspects of cellular organization. The open question is whether specific lattice, mechanical, electrical or transport states modulate neuronal computation strongly enough to matter at circuit and behavioral scales. This redevelopment therefore organizes the theory around causal transfer functions between five levels—molecular, polymer, cellular, circuit and behavior—and requires each arrow to have a measurable gain, timescale and intervention. A classical driven-dissipative model is the mandatory baseline. A quantum description is promoted only if a quantum-sensitive observable is measured, a corresponding open-system model predicts it, and classical stochastic alternatives fail on the same data. The strongest test is mediation under selective perturbation: manipulate a microtubule variable, quantify the induced change in a cellular/neural mediator, and determine whether that mediator carries a reproducible effect to circuit or behavioral outcomes. This creates a rigorous Door between scales without assuming that the Door is quantum or nonlocal in advance.
research_question: Which microtubule variables causally influence neural computation across scales, what transfer functions connect those variables to neuronal and circuit dynamics, and is any uniquely quantum mechanism required after classical mechanical, transport and biochemical explanations are fitted?
maturity: Established biology at molecular/polymer levels; T2 multiscale causal programme; quantum-consciousness necessity unestablished

levels.name: molecular
levels.state: q: tubulin conformation, binding/PTM state, local charge/electromechanical variables

levels.name: polymer
levels.state: m: lattice strain, dynamic instability, stiffness, mode amplitudes, motor traffic

levels.name: cell
levels.state: c: transport, morphology, organelle positioning, excitability, synaptic maintenance

levels.name: circuit
levels.state: n: firing rates, oscillations, effective connectivity, metastable state

levels.name: behavior/report
levels.state: y: task performance, perception, report, state transition

classical_baseline.thermal_noise: For an equilibrium linearized mode, noise/damping must satisfy an appropriate fluctuation-dissipation relation under the model assumptions.
classical_baseline.meaning: Mechanics, thermal fluctuations and transport create testable classical predictions before any coherent quantum-information interpretation is introduced.

cross_scale_transfer.gain: G_k(omega)=|H_k(omega)| measures frequency-dependent transmission between levels
cross_scale_transfer.delay: phase[H_k]/omega provides a transfer-delay estimate where the linear approximation is appropriate
cross_scale_transfer.rule: Each claimed cross-scale mechanism must estimate at least one transfer gain or causal effect rather than relying on thematic resemblance.

mediation_model.direct_effect_test: Compare a model y~q+controls with y~q+m+c+n+controls; disappearance/reduction of q's coefficient after validated mediators is evidence consistent with mediation, not proof by itself.
mediation_model.interventional_target: ATE_q->y=E[y|do(q=q1)]-E[y|do(q=q0)] for a meaningful experimentally manipulable q
mediation_model.selectivity: A valid manipulation must distinguish the candidate microtubule mechanism from generalized cytotoxicity, membrane damage or broad metabolic suppression.

information_bridge.transfer_entropy_neighbor: TE_{q->n}=I(q_past;n_future|n_past) as an observational directional-information statistic
information_bridge.warning: Transfer entropy or conditional mutual information does not establish causal mechanism without intervention or justified causal assumptions.
information_bridge.promotion: Use information measures to locate potentially useful cross-scale variables, then test them by perturbation.

quantum_branch.coherence: C(t) may be quantified with a declared off-diagonal/coherence measure appropriate to the prepared state and basis
quantum_branch.timescale_gate: tau_coh/tau_int must be large enough for the proposed operation, but this is necessary rather than sufficient.
quantum_branch.quantum_witness: Specify a witness, interference signature, spectroscopy feature or state-tomographic quantity that cannot be reproduced by the fitted classical stochastic model.
quantum_branch.model_selection: Compare quantum and classical likelihood/predictive performance on the quantum-sensitive observable, penalizing additional parameters.
quantum_branch.boundary: Neural synchrony, subjective unity or long-range correlation are not quantum witnesses.

circuit_embedding.microtubule_entry: The cellular mediator c changes an explicit circuit parameter such as gain g, effective coupling W, excitability threshold or transport-dependent synaptic efficacy.
circuit_embedding.test: Estimate whether including c improves prediction of circuit dynamics and whether selective microtubule perturbation changes the predicted parameter in the declared direction.
circuit_embedding.value: This makes the molecular-to-circuit bridge an identifiable model component instead of a verbal leap.

experimental_program: Characterize classical microtubule mechanical/electrical/transport dynamics under physiological conditions.
Identify a molecular/polymer variable with a reproducible downstream cellular correlate.
Use selective perturbation to estimate the cross-scale causal effect and rule out generic damage.
Embed the cellular effect into an explicit neuronal/circuit model and test held-out prediction.
If a quantum branch remains motivated, measure a genuinely quantum-sensitive observable and fit an open-system model.
Demonstrate that the best classical stochastic model fails on that observable before invoking quantum necessity.
Link the validated circuit effect to behavior/report through preregistered intervention outcomes and replicate.
failure_conditions: No reproducible molecular/polymer variable predicts or causes a downstream neural effect at physiological amplitudes.
Observed effects are explained by broad cytoskeletal toxicity or transport collapse.
The cross-scale transfer gain is too small/slow to influence the proposed neural computation.
Quantum-sensitive measurements are explained by classical or semiclassical stochastic models with equal or better predictive performance.
No mediation path reaches circuit/behavioral variables after confounders and measurement uncertainty are modeled.
project_boundary: Microtubules can be a scientifically meaningful cross-scale Door because they physically couple molecular, structural and transport processes. That does not establish a spiritual, telepathic or nonlocal quantum Door without separate evidence.
